title: Senior Electronics Maintenance Warrant Officer
raw_text:
8-948E. Military Occupational Specialty 948E—Senior Electronics Maintenance Warrant
Officer
    a. Licensing/certification requirement. None.
    b. Prerequisites. Demonstrated proficiency in MOS 948B or 948D. AR 135-100, DA PAM 601-
6, and DA PAM 611-21
    c. MOS 948E. MOS 948E is a non-accession MOS. The Warrant Officer feeder MOSs are:
MOS 948B and MOS 948D.
    d. Associated SQI.
         (1) 0--No special qualifications.
         (2) 8--Instructor.
         (3) P--Parachutist.
         (4) T--Transition.
         (5) Z--Research, Development, Test and Evaluation Technician.
    e. Associated ASI. Refer to DA PAM 611-21 table 6-6 (listing of universal ASIs associated
with all Warrant Officer MOSs)
    f. Qualifications.
         (1) W01/CW2 must see MOS 948B or MOS 948D.
         (2) CW3 must see MOS 948B or MOS 948D.
         (3) CW4 must see MOS 948B or MOS 948D.
         (4) CW5 must:
             (a) Meet the qualifications as listed in paragraph f (1,2, 3) above.
             (b) Successfully complete the Warrant Officer Senior Service Education (WOSSE).
             (c) Successfully perform at the CW4 level as described in paragraphs g(1, 2, 3) below.
    g. Duties.
         (1) W01/CW2 must see MOS 948B or MOS 948D.
         (2) CW3 must see MOS 948B or MOS 948D.
         (3) CW4 must see MOS 948B or MOS 948D
         (4) CW5:
             (a) Is proficient in the duties described for the CW4 level in paragraphs g(3) above.
             (b) Manages various maintenance programs to include directing assembly line
techniques, repair, and supply procedures appropriate to mobile, fixed, and depot shop conditions
in the repair/rebuild of electronic systems and other depot activities.
             (c) Coordinates contracting, procurement, and material acquisition programs and
manages the development of training packages to ensure that Army personnel are prepared to
operate and maintain new systems prior to fielding.
             (d) Administers personnel management matters pertaining to CMFs 91 and 94;
integrates electronics maintenance technical functions across MACOM or Department of the
Army levels; oversees the MOS Life Cycle Management for all personnel proponent functions, for
all Electronics Maintenance Ordnance Corps Warrant Officer MOS and serves as the electronic
maintenance system or personnel integrator at MACOM or personnel proponent level.
             (e) Serves as technical and tactical advisor for electronics systems at any echelon of
command or support activity of the U.S. Army or in Military Advisory Groups assigned to allied
armies and provides leadership, guidance, technical input and direction to subordinate elements,
staff agencies and field commanders up to and including theater Army level.
             (f) Manages the assignment of Electronics Maintenance Ordnance Corps Warrant
Officers worldwide.
             (g) Provides coordination between military and industry during development, testing,
and fielding of new electronic equipment
             (h) Technical advisor for the electronics equipment procurement process.
             (i) Operates within the research and development area of electronics systems.
             (j) Serves as a system or personnel integrator at MACOM or personnel proponent
level.
    h. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
         (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate (Gold).
          (2) A minimum OPAT score of (Standing Long Jump (LJ) - 0120 cm, seated Power Throw
(PT) - 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) - 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) - 0036 shuttles)
is required in Physical Demand Category “Moderate” (Gold).
         (3) The following grades are used to code positions into one of four definable skill levels:
W2 equals W01/CW2; W3 equals CW3; W4 equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The grades are
listed in the following standards of grade tables:
              (a) Table 8-948E-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
              (b) Table 8-948E-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
